newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slide after week of strong gains.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slide after week of strong gains.

text.p: Argentine bonds slumped Friday as the market stumbled in volatile activity on profit taking after a week of strong gains.
"It was negative all day," said a trader at a local bank.
This session's profit taking came after the market had risen virtually all of January and with a decline in U.S. Treasuries which pushed the 30-year yield above 6.90 percent.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.47 to 125.28 while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 3/4 to 88-3/4.
Earlier in the week, the market had been boosted by Argentina's $2.0 billion, 20-year global bond which was placed at a spread of 462.5 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
With the bond, the government has already raised $4.0 billion of the total $8.5 billion it said it will issue this year to cover 1997 spending needs.
But with that issue well out of the way "I can see more volatility in coming days," said another trader. "And the volatility will lead to caution."
But, "the market's fundamentals haven't changed," said the first trader, promising that the market is set to regain its upward momentum again at some point.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.50 percent from 5.65 percent.
